podcast.body: The debut album by Billy Talent features the song "This Is How It Goes," which is explicitly about drummer Aaron Solowoniuk's battle with Multiple Sclerosis. "The first song on the very first Billy Talent album is actually about Aaron and his MS."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album marked the beginning of the band's major label career in the fall of 2003. It was recorded in Vancouver with local Toronto producer Gavin Brown. The album featured songs that had been worked on for "years and years," though some, like "River Below," were written more quickly. The band's distinctive sound, particularly the singing and guitar playing, made it stand out on Canadian radio. Singles like "Try Honesty" and "River Below" were released. The album's success in Canada was boosted by high rotation on MuchMusic and an increase in the Canadian content requirement for radio to 35%. However, in the US, after "Try Honesty" did well, the label chose not to release another single, marking "the beginning of our open battle with America." "Billy Town is nothing to lose from their self-tapped major label debut album."
